Text: Move belt surfaces and goods. Turn this off if a large belt network costs too much frame time. Defaults to on.
A straight one-way belt. This is the only piece that takes goods from a building or puts goods into one.
The first one moved a single log. They kept it anyway.
Turns a belt 90°. Flip it to choose the turn. Connects to other conveyor pieces only.
Every warehouse has one corner nobody planned for.
A straight belt that fills the whole tile. It still carries one line of goods. Blocks water, paths, and pipes. You can build on top of it.
They asked for a belt and a levee. They got both, and only one of them moves.
Three inputs, one output. Each tick it takes one good from the next input that has one and puts it on the output belt.
Three lines in. One argument about whose log goes first.
One input, three outputs: left, straight, and right. Sends one good per tick to the next output that can take it.
Left, middle, right. The log does not get a vote.
Same three outputs as a splitter. Each output can take one good, any good, or overflow only. Overflow is used when a matching output is full or missing.
It is smart enough to sort. It is not smart enough to explain itself.
Sends goods between a horizontal belt and the belt directly above. Build a riser from here to climb.
The belt ends. The log does not.
Sends goods between a horizontal belt and the belt directly below. Place it on a riser or a lift up.
Down is the easy direction. The belt still wants power.
A vertical belt that carries goods upward. Build the next one from the panel.
A vertical belt that carries goods downward. Build the next one from the panel.
Gravity offered to help. The belt declined and billed for power anyway.
Belt is holding a good it cannot pass on.
Place this on a lift or a riser.
Place this on a riser or a lift up.
Conveyor belts carry solid goods. Straight belts load and unload buildings. Mergers, splitters, and lifts hand one good across each tick.
